title: Lena and the Contact
premise: Kestrel Zhou, a hostage negotiator who once talked a standoff into a massacre, has spent three years buried in a border town under a borrowed name. When her dead handler's calendar pings her with a meeting set for tomorrow at the Verraz checkpoint, she realizes the man who trained her faked his death to hand her the one file that could burn all three governments complicit in the smuggling ring she was forced to negotiate for. Hunted by an assassin who knew her before the lie began, Kestrel must run the file through a chain of reluctant witnesses to the checkpoint itself, where shifting guards offer her only a narrow window. She trades her anonymity—and nearly her life—to force the truth into daylight, ending with the ring exposed but Kestrel walking away with nothing left of the woman she invented.
about_author: Hazel Almeida is a former crisis-line counselor who writes thrillers about people who talk for a living and die for it too. She lives near a border she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Kestrel Zhou, living quietly as a translator in the border town of Solmara, receives a calendar invite from her handler Marcus Reeve—dead eleven months. POV: Kestrel. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve as she unpacks a go-bag she swore she'd never open again and admits the lie was always temporary.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Window
chapters.summary: Kestrel traces the invite to a dead-drop protocol only Reeve used, finding a burner phone with one message: the Verraz checkpoint, tomorrow, shift change. POV: Kestrel. The emotional beat is grief curdling into suspicion—either Reeve is alive, or someone is using his ghost as bait.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Her Name
chapters.summary: An assassin called Ilan Voss intercepts Kestrel at her apartment; he doesn't kill her because he recognizes her from the failed negotiation that made them both disposable. POV: alternating Kestrel and Voss. The beat is terrifying intimacy—her hunter knows exactly who she was before the lie.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One File
chapters.summary: Escaping Voss, Kestrel decrypts Reeve's cache: proof that officials in all three border nations laundered hostages through the smuggling ring she once negotiated with. POV: Kestrel. The beat is cold fury—the failure on her board wasn't hers alone; it was engineered.

chapters.title: What Amara Owed
chapters.summary: Kestrel seeks Amara Diallo, a disgraced journalist who owes Reeve a debt, to authenticate the file before dawn. POV: Amara. The beat is wary alliance—Amara wants the story, Kestrel wants leverage, and neither trusts the other with the whole truth.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Voss closes in, forcing Kestrel and Amara onto freight routes toward Verraz while the checkpoint's guard rotation gives them a forty-minute window. POV: Kestrel. The beat is hunted momentum—every shortcut Reeve built into her training now doubles as a trap someone else knows.

chapters.title: The Negotiation She Never Finished
chapters.summary: Cornered at a rail yard, Kestrel does what she does best: negotiates—with Voss, offering him exposure of his own handlers in exchange for passage. POV: alternating Kestrel and Voss. The beat is dangerous hope as two survivors realize they were built by the same machine.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Verraz
chapters.summary: At the checkpoint, Kestrel finds not Reeve but his final recording, plus a live feed rigged to broadcast if she dies there. POV: Kestrel. The beat is devastating clarity—Reeve's meeting invitation was a dead man's switch, and she was always the trigger.

chapters.title: Everything on the Table
chapters.summary: Ring enforcers storm the checkpoint; Kestrel bargains seconds into minutes, broadcasting the file while Voss holds the line against men he once served. POV: alternating Kestrel and Voss. The climax beat: she talks her way through gunfire, spending every skill she has on the truth instead of a life.

chapters.title: After the Broadcast
chapters.summary: The file goes public; arrests ripple across three capitals while Kestrel, wounded and unrecognizable even to herself, crosses the border legally for the first time in years. POV: Kestrel. The resolution beat: justice outside the law cost her the lie, and she discovers that surviving without it might be livable after all.
